results.name: Wrist Curl Barbell
instructions: Kneel on the floor in front of a bench, placing both forearms over the bench while holding a barbell with an underhand grip (palms facing up).
Rest your wrists just off the edge of the bench, allowing the barbell to hang downward.
Curl the barbell upward by flexing your wrists, lifting it as high as possible while keeping your forearms flat on the bench.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position, fully extending your wrists. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your forearms pressed firmly against the bench to isolate the wrist movement.
Use a controlled motion to lift and lower the barbell, avoiding any jerking movements.
Avoid using your shoulder or upper arm to lift the weight.
results.description: Wrist Curl Barbell is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Alternate Heel Touch Side Kick Squat
instructions: Stand tall with your back straight, arms by your side, and feet shoulder-width apart.
Lower your hips by bending one of your knees while sliding the opposite leg outward on the floor, and touch your heel with your hands.
Return to the initial position, and do the same while bending your other knee and sliding the opposite leg.
tips: Keep your core engaged to maintain balance and stability throughout the exercise.
Ensure your knees do not extend past your toes when squatting to protect your joints.
Perform the side leg slides with controlled movements to maintain proper form and avoid injury.
results.description: Alternate Heel Touch Side Kick Squat is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Adductors, Abductors.

results.name: Alternating Step Out
instructions: Stand tall with your back straight and your feet shoulder-width apart.
Bend your knees slightly and clasp your hands in front of your chest.
Lift one of your feet off the floor and step to your side.
Return to the initial position and do the same with your other foot. Repeat.
tips: Focus on keeping your upper body upright and avoid leaning too far forward or backward.
Use a steady pace to maintain a rhythm, which will help with coordination and balance.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you step out and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
results.description: Alternating Step Out is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abductors, Adductors.

results.name: Ankle Pumps
instructions: Sit or lie with your legs straight.
Point your toes away from you as far as you comfortably can.
Pull your toes back toward your shins.
Keep alternating in a slow, steady rhythm.
tips: Useful for circulation and ankle mobility.
Move through the full range.
results.description: Ankle Pumps is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category.

results.name: Assisted Bulgarian Split Squat
instructions: Stand facing away from an elevated box and place your right foot on it. Hold onto a stable bar or support in front of you with your right hand. Keep your chest upright and your front foot flat on the floor.
Lower your body by bending your front knee and hip until your back knee is close to the floor.
Pause for a second at the bottom and push through the heel of your front foot to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired repetitions, then switch legs and repeat.
tips: Use the support only for balance, not to pull yourself up.
Do not let your front knee travel excessively past your toes to reduce joint stress.
Maintain an upright torso to keep the tension on your quads and glutes.
results.description: Assisted Bulgarian Split Squat is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

results.name: Assisted Pistol Squats
instructions: Stand upright while holding onto a sturdy equipment with both hands for balance. Extend one leg straight forward and keep it off the floor while the other leg remains on the floor.
Lower yourself slowly by bending the standing leg at the hip and knee, keeping your chest up and your extended leg straight in front of you.
Descend until your glutes are close to your heel and then push through the heel of your planted foot to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired repetitions, then switch legs and repeat.
tips: Lower yourself slowly and avoid collapsing at the bottom of the squat to avoid injury.
Extend your non-working leg fully in front of you and keep it parallel to the floor.
Use your arms only for assistance, not to pull yourself up or down.
results.description: Assisted Pistol Squats is an advanced multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.
